overview.title: Union Budgets On Agriculture
overview.definition: The systematic allocation of fiscal resources, capital expenditures, subsidies, and policy incentives directed by the Government of India through the annual Union Budget toward the primary sector to ensure food security, enhance rural livelihoods, and boost agricultural productivity.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for GS Paper III (Indian Economy, Agriculture, Resource Mobilization, Inclusive Growth) and Prelims (schemes, budget allocations, institutional credit, and capital formation trends).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Union Budgets On Agriculture.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Shift from Price Support to Income Support**: Evolution of Union Budget allocations from heavily relying on input subsidies (fertilizer, power, irrigation) toward direct income transfers such as **PM-KISAN**.
• **Capital vs. Revenue Expenditure**: Budgets increasingly differentiate between recurring revenue expenditures (subsidies, waivers) and asset-creating capital expenditures (**Agriculture Infrastructure Fund - AIF**, cold chains, irrigation).
• **Institutional Credit Target**: Annual budgetary targets set for priority sector lending (PSL) and institutional credit flow through NABARD, commercial banks, and cooperative societies.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Share of agriculture and allied sectors in total budgetary allocation versus its contribution to Gross Value Added (GVA).

items.definition: Budgetary provision providing short-term crop loans to farmers at subsidized interest rates (7% base reduced to 4% for timely repayment).
A medium-long term debt financing facility for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
State Plan Scheme of overarching nature allowing states to choose their own agriculture and allied sector development projects based on district plans.
Dalwai Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income, MS Swaminathan Commission recommendations, Essential Commodities Act amendments.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **North-Western Plains (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP)**: Historically highest concentration of procurement-led budget allocations and power/fertilizer subsidies.
• **Eastern & North-Eastern States**: Focus of recent budgetary pushes for second green revolution, oil palm missions, and organic farming clusters.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High fiscal burden of recurring subsidies crowding out capital expenditure; skewed regional benefits.
• **Policy Interventions**: Diversification toward millets (Shree Anna), digital public infrastructure for agriculture (AgriStack), and natural farming promotion.

items.title: Mnemonic for Major Agricultural Budget Pillars
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'C.I.S.R' -> Credit, Infrastructure, Subsidies, Resilience.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Credit (Institutional loans), Infrastructure (AIF/Cold chains), Subsidies (Fertilizer/Power), Resilience (PMFBY/Climate smart).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Quickly categorizes budgetary announcements in MCQs.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Whenever a budget shifts from price-based interventions to direct income support (like PM-KISAN), fiscal efficiency improves while market distortion reduces.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'All agricultural subsidies are fully funded by the Central Government.' This is incorrect, as several schemes (like PMFBY and RKVY) operate on a Central-State cost-sharing ratio (e.g., 60:40 or 90:10 for North-Eastern states).

Mains Value Addition: Argue for 're-allocative efficiency' in the budget—moving funds away from input-heavy subsidies (power/fertilizer leading to water table depletion and soil degradation) toward agri-R&D, extension services, and digital public infrastructure.

keyTakeaways: Union Budgets are critical instruments transitioning Indian agriculture from subsistence to commercial and sustainable models.
A healthy balance between revenue expenditure (subsidies) and capital expenditure (infrastructure) is vital for long-term agricultural GVA growth.
Digital initiatives and climate-resilient allocations dominate modern budget cycles to counter agrarian distress and climate change.
